reason: Opening zip/cbz straight in a viewer is the one thing that interests me, since Photos can't do it. But I would not hand over my default to a 0.4.1 from one person, so it stays a second app for comics.
why_switch_or_not: I would install it for the cbz/zip support and the speed on big folders, and open a few of my comic archives to see how it handles hundreds of pages. Nothing in the description says it has a manga reading mode (page spreads, right-to-left, remembering my place), so I don't know it would beat what I do now. My catalogue, XMP and colour setup cannot break, and a version 0.4.1 from a single developer is not something I will make the default.
current_app_pros: Windows Photos is already there, opens on double-click, and never asks me anything. For a single picture it is fine. My catalogue and colour setup stay untouched because Photos doesn't interfere with them.
current_app_pains: It can't open zip or cbz, so I have to extract archives first or use something else for comics. It is slow to start and slow when I flip through big folders.
objection: Another image viewer, from one developer, at version 0.4.1. If it crashes on a 400-page archive or breaks how my files are handled, I lose time, and I don't know if it will still be maintained in a year.
would_change_my_mind: A proper comic-reading mode (right-to-left, double-page, resume where I stopped) that works on big cbz files without hiccups, plus a few months of stable releases.
